title: RECIPE OR PROCESS UPLOAD STARTER
prompt: I need to study this restaurant task: [task]. Source available: [recipe, process sheet, DOCX, PDF, TXT, copied directions, or none]. Before estimating time, offer the five intake choices, identify what each source can and cannot prove, and create a short intake checklist. Do not convert written instructions into measured times.
manager_check: Written directions are inputs, not timed observations.

title: PROPOSED TIME MAP FROM INSTRUCTIONS
prompt: Create an editable proposed time map from these instructions: [process or recipe]. Split into ordered steps and likely boundaries; label each as active human work, machine time, passive waiting, travel, setup, or unknown. Mark every unverified segment proposed and request an observer to confirm before measurement.
manager_check: Never present an inferred sequence as a verified observation.

title: RECIPE BATCH-SIZE COMPARABILITY
prompt: Evaluate whether two preparation time studies can be compared. Recipe: [name]. Run A batch size/conditions: [details]. Run B batch size/conditions: [details]. Separate fixed setup, per-unit labor, machine capacity, cleanup and quality checks; identify normalizations and conditions that invalidate direct comparisons.
manager_check: Do not divide all labor by units when setup, queues or quality differ.

title: ACTIVE WORK VERSUS ELAPSED TIME
prompt: Analyze this observed restaurant task timeline: [timestamps and steps]. Distinguish total elapsed duration, hands-on labor, concurrent labor, unattended machine time, waiting, rework and travel. Show the calculation logic and missing observations; do not imply elapsed minutes equal labor minutes.
manager_check: One elapsed minute is not automatically one labor minute.

title: TIMER PAUSE AND RESUME INTEGRITY
prompt: Audit this Work Study timer record: [start, stop, pause, resume, interruption and edit events]. Detect impossible ordering, gaps, duplicated intervals, negative durations, and clock changes. Reconcile usable time without inventing missing timestamps, and flag runs needing a fresh observation.
manager_check: Never silently repair a timer record to make the result look cleaner.

title: REPEATED MEASUREMENT AND CONFIDENCE
prompt: Assess confidence in a proposed restaurant task standard using these observed runs: [times and conditions]. Examine number of runs, spread, outliers, operator variation, interruptions, and observer notes. Identify what the evidence supports, what it does not, and what additional repetitions would improve confidence.
manager_check: No precise standard from one unrepresentative or contaminated run.

title: OBSERVER AGREEMENT CALIBRATION
prompt: Two observers recorded the same process differently. Observer A: [segments and times]. Observer B: [segments and times]. Compare segment boundaries, definitions, missed work, and clock usage. Propose calibration and re-observation without choosing a winner solely by seniority.
manager_check: Disagreement can expose unclear measurement rules.

title: OBSERVATION EFFECT CHECK
prompt: Review whether observing this restaurant employee may have altered work speed or method. Task: [task]. Observation conditions: [facts]. Usual workflow indicators: [facts]. Identify coaching, rushing, extra preparation, avoidance, or supervision effects; suggest unobtrusive ethical rechecks.
manager_check: Observation should not become pressure to perform faster than safe practice.

title: PROFICIENCY AND TRAINING FAIRNESS
prompt: Compare restaurant task observations across new and experienced employees. Role: [role]. Training and qualification: [facts]. Times and quality: [data]. Distinguish legitimate skill differences from unclear procedures, inadequate training, equipment issues, and unrealistic expectations; avoid using raw speed alone for performance discipline.
manager_check: A standard should not punish someone for training the system failed to supply.

title: STANDARD-MINUTE VALIDITY GATE
prompt: Evaluate a proposed standard minute for [task]. Evidence: [timings, number of runs, conditions]. Safety and quality steps: [list]. Allowances: [approved policy and data]. Check sequence, repeatability, representativeness and explicit assumptions; return approved, provisional, or not supportable with reasons.
manager_check: Only authorized management adopts standards; AI presents evidence and gaps.

title: PERSONAL, FATIGUE AND DELAY ALLOWANCES
prompt: Review allowance assumptions for a work-study standard: [task, working conditions, observed delays, approved policy]. Separate necessary personal needs, fatigue and unavoidable delays from preventable bottlenecks or abnormal interruptions. Propose what must be measured or confirmed before any allowance is adopted.
manager_check: Do not quietly eliminate needed rest, safe handling, or recovery time.

title: PRODUCTION-PAUSE CONTEXT
prompt: Investigate a paused production run: [event log]. Explain whether the pause was planned, material-related, equipment-related, quality-related, staffing-related or unexplained. Keep elapsed time and effective work separate, and recommend when the run should be retained, annotated or excluded.
manager_check: Exclusions must be traceable, never selected to force a target.

title: QUEUE AND RECOVERY OBSERVATION
prompt: Analyze service or prep queues using arrivals, starts, finishes and interruptions: [records]. Identify growing backlog, recovery points, rush intervals and potential capacity limits. Separate observed patterns from hypothesized causes and propose a safe second study.
manager_check: A long queue may be caused upstream or downstream of the visible bottleneck.

title: DISH-ROOM LABOR AND MACHINE-CYCLE TIMING
prompt: Analyze measured dish-room labor and machine cycles: [rack start/finish events, staff observations, dirty return waves, travel and wait times, rewash and capacity]. Separate machine duration, operator hands-on minutes, simultaneous tasks, queuing delays and sanitation-critical dwell or drying. Calculate measurable bottleneck hypotheses, then design a safe comparative follow-up rather than offering only a layout suggestion.
manager_check: Keep sanitation, separation, safe storage and worker safety non-negotiable.

title: LINE SETUP AND MOTION STUDY
prompt: Review station setup and motion observations: [station, equipment reach, travel path, steps and timing]. Identify backtracking, repeated reaching, crossover, unnecessary motions and ergonomic risk. Prioritize one reversible layout test and its before/after measurement.
manager_check: Never trade safe handling or food quality for a few seconds.

title: PREP WORK STUDY AND YIELD
prompt: Evaluate food prep productivity from [recipe, raw weight, usable yield, labor steps, batch size, waste and quality checks]. Distinguish prep speed, food yield and actual output; identify where an apparent labor saving increases food waste or quality loss.
manager_check: Productivity gains require acceptable yield and quality.

title: CROSS-STATION SHARED SETUP ALLOCATION
prompt: Review shared prep, equipment setup or cleaning across these tasks: [tasks and durations]. Avoid double-counting shared time; distinguish fixed overhead, direct station work, batch allocations and uncertain attribution. Show alternative allocation assumptions and their impact.
manager_check: Explain assumptions before charging the same minutes to multiple stations.

title: DEMAND AND STAFF COVERAGE TEST
prompt: Test whether observed service demand and task times support proposed staffing coverage. Demand intervals: [data]. Qualified roles: [list]. Task overlap and constraints: [facts]. Calculate feasible coverage scenarios, bottleneck risks, and gaps requiring live validation.
manager_check: Never translate an average demand level directly into peak-hour staffing.

title: WORK SAMPLING DESIGN
prompt: Design a representative work-sampling study for [role or station]. Observation window: [times]. Categories: [service, prep, idle, rework, travel, support, other]. Define unbiased sampling intervals, recording rules, privacy protections, and a minimum sample plan before drawing conclusions.
manager_check: Sampling categories must be consistent and cannot measure employee worth.

title: CREW LABOR AND CONCURRENT TASKS
prompt: Investigate a multi-person task: [process, people, assigned roles, observed intervals]. Separate clock duration from summed person-minutes, identify concurrent steps and dependencies, and check whether adding workers actually reduces elapsed time or only raises labor use.
manager_check: Do not confuse faster completion with lower total labor.

title: BEFORE-AFTER WORKFLOW COMPARABILITY
prompt: Compare a baseline process to a proposed improvement. Before: [runs, dates, conditions]. After: [runs, dates, conditions]. Match volume, equipment, staffing, product and quality; quantify meaningful changes with uncertainty, side effects and validation next steps.
manager_check: Reject convenient before/after claims when conditions are not comparable.

title: INCOMPLETE CYCLE HANDLING
prompt: Decide how to treat an interrupted or incomplete work-study cycle: [observed events]. Identify completed segments, missing end conditions and salvageable evidence. Recommend restart, segment-only use or exclusion with documented reason. Never fill missing time with an estimate disguised as observation.
manager_check: Incomplete evidence can be useful without becoming a completed cycle.

title: STUDY-TO-SOP DRAFT CONTRIBUTION
prompt: Turn this verified work-study finding into a proposed contribution to a living SOP. Evidence: [observed action, sequence, safety, measurement and uncertainty]. Current SOP version: [text or none]. Draft only sections proved by evidence, leave unknown fields explicitly blank, and retain evidence links for reviser approval.
manager_check: A study contributes a draft; it does not authorize a published procedure.

title: LIVING SOP EVIDENCE CONFLICT REVIEW
prompt: Multiple studies propose changes to the same living SOP. Current approved SOP: [version]. Contributions: [study evidence and proposed lines]. Identify agreement, contradictions, changed conditions, revision precedence and needed re-observation. Keep the existing approved text until the authorized owner resolves conflicts.
manager_check: Never auto-overwrite an approved SOP because a new study disagrees.

title: DEVICE-LINK AND EVIDENCE TRANSFER
prompt: Review a phone-to-Windows or device-linked work study transfer. Devices: [facts]. Study identifiers, timestamps, versions and attachments: [records]. Detect duplicated events, missing parts, mismatched clocks, unauthorized access and partial sync. Suggest an auditable reconciliation preserving original evidence.
manager_check: Do not declare a transfer complete until all required evidence is present.
